name: Battle of the Teutoburg Forest

phases.title: The Bructeri strike the strung-out column
phases.text: The Roman army moved through thick forest, its line of march stretched over 15 to 20 kilometres. The Bructeri attacked along its length with javelins, a brief skirmish meant to tire the Romans and damage their supplies. The Angrivarii lay hidden at Kalkriese.

phases.title: The Bructeri withdraw and the Romans camp
phases.text: The Bructeri withdrew quickly. A torrential downpour left the Romans unable to advance, and Varus ordered the army to make camp. Losses reported were light, but the baggage trains and scout cavalry were shown to be vulnerable.

phases.title: A night march into the second trap
phases.text: The Romans marched at night to escape and went into another trap set at the foot of Kalkriese Hill. There the open strip they could march along was squeezed to a gap of about 100 metres between the woods and the swampland at the edge of the Great Bog.

phases.title: The Romans try to storm the wall
phases.text: The road was blocked by a trench and an earthen wall built along its side, which let the Germanic alliance attack from cover. The Romans made a desperate attempt to storm the wall and failed.

phases.title: Vala rides off and is overtaken
phases.text: The highest-ranking officer next to Varus, Numonius Vala, abandoned the troops by riding off with the cavalry. Germanic cavalry overtook him and he was killed shortly afterwards, according to Velleius Paterculus.

phases.title: The Germanic warriors storm the field
phases.text: The Germanic warriors stormed the field and cut down the disintegrating Roman forces. Varus killed himself. By later accounts some officers were sacrificed or ransomed and some common soldiers enslaved.

note: The plan shows the march and the ambush near Kalkriese, a possible site of the battle. The accounts do not say which way the road ran, how the Roman column was ordered along it, or where the woods, the wall and the trench lay beyond what they state, so their places are set by judgement. The cavalry's line of flight is not given. The battle ran from 8 to 11 September 9 CE; the plan shows only its main stages.
